corpora.name: human-shops
corpora.what: Product descriptions taken from Wayback Machine snapshots of eight Spanish-language shops: Mr. Wonderful (136, Spain), DaWanda Spain (88), Artesanio (87, Spain), Regalador (44, Spain), Monoblock (35, Argentina), the Mendoza social-economy catalogue (32, Argentina), Cuidado con el Perro (32, Mexico) and Complot (4, Argentina). DaWanda and Artesanio are small sellers, the Mendoza catalogue small businesses, the rest brands with copywriters. Texts shorter than 120 characters, mostly non-Spanish texts and duplicates were dropped.
corpora.dates: Snapshots from 2012-01-20 to 2022-08-19, all before November 2022
corpora.license: Each text belongs to its shop, so only URL, snapshot, date, length and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: Small and mostly from Spain (355). Mr. Wonderful has a strong voice and weighs a lot. Some DaWanda texts are machine translations by foreign sellers and some are cut-off meta descriptions. The patterns were tuned while looking at this set, so its false-positive rate is optimistic.

corpora.name: autext-human
corpora.what: All human texts of the Spanish subtask 1 training set of AuTexTification 2023: legal texts, tweets and Wikipedia. Not product copy; a check against ordinary Spanish.
corpora.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only counts are shipped.
corpora.dates: Not stated by the task; undated here, so not known to be from before November 2022.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web
corpora.what: 2,000 random pages of the Spanish web: the prose paragraphs of each page (12 or more words, enough function words, few capitals; scripts/lib/prose.mjs), 40 to 1,200 words, spam keywords excluded, drawn by a seeded shuffle (seed 42) by scripts/sample-mc4-web.mjs. A check against ordinary prose of every kind.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web-holdout
corpora.what: 1,000 further pages from the same shuffle, kept back while the general candidates were chosen.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: autext-generated
corpora.what: All generated texts of the same set: BLOOM 1B to 7B, GPT-3 babbage and curie, and text-davinci-003 continuing a prompt. These models continue text instead of answering a request.
corpora.dates: Not stated by the task; undated here.

corpora.name: ai-imitation
corpora.what: Titles and descriptions for mugs, t-shirts, posters, blankets, tote bags, stickers and phone cases, generated with Claude in the default listing style of chat assistants, for Spain, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Chile.
corpora.caveats: Written with the candidate patterns in view, so recall here is inflated.

corpora.name: ai-sonnet
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet answering 70 seller requests (Spain 28, Mexico 14, Argentina 14, Colombia 7, Chile 7) with no style instructions. The request is stored with each text.

corpora.name: ai-haiku
corpora.what: Claude Haiku answering the same 70 requests.

corpora.name: ai-general
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering plain requests in six genres (blog post, email to colleagues, short essay, newspaper article, LinkedIn post, short report) on eight everyday topics, made by scripts/generate-general.mjs from scripts/general-requests.json. The models saw no pattern list. The general entries added in 0.2.0 were drawn from this set and the ones revised in 0.3.0 were tuned on it, so its hit rates overstate recall; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are the clean held-out measure.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. Claude Code put the account's email address in the context, and Sonnet signed 11 emails across the three languages with the account owner's name; that name was replaced by a neutral one and the rows carry a 'redacted' note. The model ids were not recorded at generation; each row carries the id the alias resolved to with the same CLI version on the same day.

corpora.name: ai-general-holdout
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering the requests in scripts/general-requests-holdout.json: the same six genres as ai-general, eight new topics. Written after the 0.2.0 general entries were chosen. Its results were read during the 0.3.0 review rounds, so it is no longer a clean held-out estimate; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are. Each row records the resolved model id and the system prompt, which tells the model to ignore the account email in its context.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. One Spanish reply (email-8-sonnet) still used the account owner's name despite the system prompt; it was discarded and the request sent again, and the row records discarded: 1.

corpora.name: ai-multi-holdout
corpora.what: Six models answering plain one-line requests from scripts/multi-requests.json: seven genres (blog post, email to friends, short essay, local newspaper article, Instagram post, short report, and a long article of about 800 words) on eight everyday topics that appear in no other corpus. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 56 requests each (224 texts). OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23) answered the six short genres on the first topic (6 texts) and GPT-5.4 mini (gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17) the six short genres on the first four topics (24 texts). Sent through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages APIs by scripts/generate-api.mjs with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit: the models saw only the request and never a pattern list. Each row records the generator, provider, resolved model id, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: OpenAI is kept small for budget: 30 of 254 texts, two models, no long form, so the GPT rows show direction only. Every reply ended normally (stop or end_turn) and is at least 200 characters long. The Claude rows were checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

corpora.name: ai-detailed-holdout
corpora.what: Realistic requests with concrete facts, as people type them to a chat assistant: 56 scenarios (eight per genre, the same seven genres as ai-multi-holdout, outlined in scripts/detailed-scenarios.md), each written twice in the language, as a short request (style A, one or two sentences) and a careful one (style B, with audience, tone, length and the facts as notes), in scripts/detailed-requests/es.json. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 112 requests each, through the Anthropic Message Batches API (scripts/generate-api.mjs batch) with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit. Half the scenarios are set in Spain (224 texts) and half in Latin America: Argentina 80, Mexico 72, Colombia 72; each row carries the variety. Each row records the generator, resolved model id, style, scenario, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only. The requests were written for this study by a model that did not see the pattern lists, following the scenario outline; names, places, addresses and contact details in them are invented. Every reply ended with end_turn and was checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates.
